_provenance: Hand-labelled by the repository owner on 2026-08-24 after watching tt6.mp4.
The seven 'actions' below are the owner's own words and choices, unedited.
This is the only ground truth the project has. Do not 'improve' it to make
a score look better -- if it disagrees with the pipeline, the pipeline is
what is wrong.
tt6.mp4 is ONE 6.667s recording copied FIVE times end to end. The labels
describe the source clip once; tools/score_run.py expands them x5 by adding
i * source_clip_duration_sec. So ground truth for the whole video is 35
actions.
This file first said four copies of 8.3s, obtained by dividing 33.2s by an
assumed count. That was wrong, and wrong invisibly: score_run.py offsets
each copy's labels by the period and audit_detections.py folds frames modulo
it, so both tools kept reporting numbers while placing copies 2-4 up to 4.9s
away from the footage they were scoring, and never scoring copy 5 at all.
The corrected values come from pixels, not arithmetic. tools/align_clips.py
slides tt7.mp4 (200 frames, the source clip on its own) along tt6.mp4 and
reports mean grey difference per offset. Result: matches at frames 0, 199,
at non-copy offset 498 and a 28.8 worst case. Offset 0 is bit-identical, so
tt7.mp4 IS tt6.mp4 frames 0-199 and these label times need no shift.
Copy stride is therefore 199 frames (6.6333s), not tt7's own 200 frames:
5 x 200 = 1000 against tt6's 996, i.e. one frame is dropped at each of the
four seams. source_clip_duration_sec is the STRIDE, because that is what
score_run.py multiplies. Its worst per-copy error is one frame (copy 4,
predicted 19.900s vs actual 19.933s), far inside timing_tolerance_sec.
_known_limitations: action 'FOLD' is NOT in src/schema/event.py ActionType. The vocabulary has
no word for folding a box flap, which is a real gap for packing tasks, not
a labelling mistake. The scorer reports it as NOT_IN_VOCABULARY rather than
action 7 uses direction 'OFF' for lifting the box and moving it aside. The
template offered no value for a lateral move. That is a shortcoming of the
template, and 'OFF' is kept as written.

actions.note: end clamped from 7.0 to the 6.633s clip end. The source clip is 6.667s and its copy stride 6.633s, so an end of 7.0 ran past the cut into the next copy; the move itself is truncated by the edit, not re-timed.
